segments.title: 第16章 優秀畢業生
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years Chapter 16: Outstanding Graduates

June 28th, three o'clock in the afternoon.

The students from the twelve third-year classes of Yucai Middle School, each carrying their own chair, filed out of the old academic building like ants, heading towards the sports field.

Ying Chanxi wasn't particularly tall, probably around one meter sixty-two.

But she was still relatively tall among the girls in her class, so when they lined up, she naturally ended up walking side-by-side with Li Luo.

Shao Heqi was lined up just in front of Li Luo. He slipped his right arm through the gap in the back of his chair, propping it on his shoulder, and easily carried it forward with one hand.

He turned his head and saw Ying Chanxi holding her chair with both hands, looking a bit awkward and struggling as she walked, so he couldn't help but offer, "Class President, you want me to carry that for you?"

"I'm fine, it's not that heavy," Ying Chanxi said, shaking her head and politely declining Shao Heqi's kind offer.

Instead, it was Jin Yuting walking ahead who was panting from exhaustion. She said to Shao Heqi, "Vice President, since you're so free, why don't you help me? I'm about to collapse."

Faced with Jin Yuting's request, Shao Heqi fell silent for a few seconds. He felt it wouldn't look good to refuse in front of Ying Chanxi, so he finally nodded and took the chair from Jin Yuting's hands.

But just as they walked from the second floor to the outside of the academic building and started heading toward the sports field, Ying Chanxi suddenly turned to Li Luo and shoved her chair into his hands, "I'm a little tired now. Li Luo, you carry this for me."

Li Luo accepted it with a speechless look on his face. "Why didn't you let Shao Heqi help you just now?"

"I wasn't tired then," Ying Chanxi said, blinking with an innocent expression. "I'm tired now."

Along the way, the sight of boys carrying chairs for girls was not uncommon, so Li Luo and Ying Chanxi's situation didn't particularly stand out.

However, upon seeing Li Luo take Ying Chanxi's chair, Shao Heqi, walking ahead, practically grit his teeth to pieces and almost stumbled into a tree by the roadside.

Especially when he remembered Li Luo's incredibly high test score, the one advantage he thought he had over him was crushed in a single blow. Shao Heqi was fuming inside.

He didn't even have the right to mock or be sarcastic to Li Luo anymore. What was the point of living?

Shao Heqi sighed deeply in his heart, looking up at the bleak leaves of the trees by the road, which rustled as they swayed in the wind as if mourning for him.

With two chairs on his shoulders, he felt like a tragic swordsman walking into the sunset, blood at the corner of his mouth, wishing for nothing more than to die in Ying Chanxi's arms while shielding her from a blade in the next moment.

Then he would live forever in her heart.

A boy in his chuunibyou phase couldn't help but fantasize about such random things.

By the time Shao Heqi came back to his senses, the class line had already reached its designated spot and students were starting to arrange their seats.

Although Ying Chanxi and Li Luo had walked out side-by-side, when it came time to sit in rows, it turned out that Jin Yuting was actually next to Li Luo.

So Ying Chanxi patted Jin Yuting's shoulder and gestured for her to switch seats, "Tingting, you'll get more sun if you sit in the front. You should sit behind me."

Jin Yuting usually followed Ying Chanxi's lead, so she naturally got up and swapped seats with her instinctively.

This left Shao Heqi, sitting in front of Li Luo, with mixed feelings.

Even though Ying Chanxi was now sitting in the same row as Li Luo, she was sitting on the chair he had just carried for Jin Yuting!

This gave him a small sense of participation, offering his heart a sliver of comfort.

...

A June day, at three in the afternoon.

On the sports field, under the blazing sun, a sea of heads bustled about.

Holding a graduation ceremony on the sports field in this kind of weather would have been truly unbearable if they hadn't been able to bring chairs down to sit on.

But even so, just sitting under the sun for a few minutes was enough to make many people break out in a sweat.

Luckily, Li Luo was smart enough to have brought a small notebook when he came downstairs. Now, he took it out and fanned himself with it, which cooled him down considerably.

"I'm hot too," Ying Chanxi said, her big eyes staring at him placidly.

Li Luo turned his head to meet her gaze, then reached out and placed the notebook in her hand.

"Fanning myself is too tiring," Ying Chanxi said, pushing the notebook back, leaving Li Luo speechless.

"So it's not tiring for me?" Li Luo rolled his eyes, took the notebook, and began fanning it in her direction.

Ying Chanxi closed her eyes, enjoying the cool breeze on her face. Her bangs were blown up slightly, revealing her smooth, full forehead.

About ten minutes later, all twelve third-year classes had assembled.

The school leaders also took their seats on the stage one after another.

Seeing the thick stacks of speech manuscripts in the hands of the principal, vice principal, and dean of students, Li Luo couldn't help but feel a headache coming on.

"What on earth is the surprise Teacher Zhang was talking about?" Li Luo complained in a low voice. "He didn't even explain it clearly, just told me to listen carefully."

"I actually have a guess," Ying Chanxi whispered back.

"What did you guess?"

"I'm not telling you," Ying Chanxi said, shaking her head with a secretive smile. "Teacher Zhang told you to listen carefully, so what's wrong with listening carefully?"

"Who knows which overworked teacher pulled an all-nighter to write those speeches for the principal and the others? Listening to this is less practical than taking a nap," Li Luo said, shaking his head and sighing.

However, once the vice principal began his speech, Li Luo didn't actually go to sleep. He obediently listened.

"Distinguished school leaders, dear teachers, and our lovely students who are about to graduate and soar!"

"At this moment filled with joy and reluctance, we gather here to witness and celebrate your successful completion of your junior high school studies, as you are about to embark on a new chapter in your lives."

"First, please allow me, on behalf of the school, to extend my warmest congratulations to all the graduates!"

After listening earnestly up to this point, Li Luo raised his hands and clapped with a helpless expression. He then continued to listen to the vice principal drone on for over half an hour, but there was still no sign of the surprise Teacher Zhang had mentioned.

After the vice principal finished, it was the dean of students' turn to speak.

Compared to the vice principal's rather empty, grandiloquent talk, the dean of students was a bit more down-to-earth.

He talked about some of the major events that had happened at the school over the past three years, reviewing the junior high school years with the students.

Afterward, the dean of students moved on to the third-year teachers, listing the excellent educational achievements of several of them and announcing the ten outstanding teachers selected by the school this year.

Among them, Teacher Zhang Wei from Class Five of the third year was on the list.

The other nine teachers were either veteran teachers who had earned it through seniority or teachers from the honors classes.

Someone like Zhang Wei, who was still relatively young and a teacher of a parallel class, stood out conspicuously among them.

"Damn! Don't tell me this is the surprise Teacher Zhang was talking about?" Li Luo watched Zhang Wei walk onto the awards stage with a smug look, feeling utterly speechless. "Did he get this award because I got into Yuhang Fuyi High School?"

"You're overthinking it," Ying Chanxi shot him a look. "The outstanding teachers were selected a while ago. Today is just the announcement."

The main reason Zhang Wei was able to receive this award was because of the existence of Ying Chanxi and Zhao Rongjun.

After all, out of more than five hundred students at Yucai Middle School, only 27 were selected for the early admission independent recruitment of Yuhang Fuyi High School.

And among these 27 students, 24 were from the honors classes.

Of the remaining three students, one was from Class Eight, and the other two were from Class Five.

That wasn't even the main point.

The main point was that Ying Chanxi had easily taken first place in the entire district in the independent recruitment exam for Yuhang Fuyi High School!

The student from the honors class who ranked second in the school, behind Ying Chanxi, was already ranked beyond twentieth place in the independent recruitment exam.

One could imagine the gap between them.

Riding on Ying Chanxi's name alone was enough for Zhang Wei to secure this outstanding teacher slot.

Not to mention he also had Zhao Rongjun as a bonus.

"When one person attains the Dao, even their chickens and dogs ascend to heaven," Li Luo muttered under his breath as he watched Zhang Wei receive the award certificate from the principal.

"What are you saying," Ying Chanxi said, not knowing whether to laugh or be angry. "Teacher Zhang is a good teacher too."

"Good students aren't taught into existence," Li Luo said, shaking his head. "As long as a good student has a good environment, they can learn very well on their own."

"And to evaluate a teacher's teaching ability, the key is to see how well they teach the students in the middle and lower tiers."

"From that perspective, ahem, I'm the one who truly makes him worthy of the 'outstanding teacher' title."

Ying Chanxi was speechless.

At first, what Li Luo said sounded quite reasonable.

But by the end, his ulterior motives were exposed.

But in fact, Li Luo wasn't wrong.

Although Zhang Wei already knew he had been selected as an outstanding teacher, he was, in essence, not entirely deserving of the title.

Because the selection of outstanding teachers at Yucai Middle School was related to future competitions for municipal and provincial-level teacher titles, most of the time, it was the high-quality teachers from the honors classes who competed for it.

The teaching abilities of teachers in parallel classes were relatively weaker.

Previously, in the eyes of many honors class teachers, Zhang Wei had purely been carried to success by his student, Ying Chanxi.

If this Ying Chanxi had been a student in any of their classes, they could have easily secured the spot.

They could only say that Zhang Wei was lucky.

But.

In this year's high school entrance exam, a freak like Li Luo appeared!

Although Li Luo's exam score was excellent, it was still only ranked 18th in the entire school.

If this had happened to a student like Shao Heqi, who consistently got good grades, there would be nothing more to say.

But this student, Li Luo, the highest score he had ever gotten before was only 425 points!

Now it was 555 points.

In the short span of a month and a half.

A huge difference of 130 points!

Moreover, he was the only student in the entire school to get a perfect score of 40 on the Chinese composition.

Besides Li Luo, the student with the biggest improvement in the entire school for this exam had only increased their total score by a little over thirty points.

One could imagine just how absurd Li Luo's situation was.

Under the halo of this achievement, even Zhang Wei's "outstanding teacher" title seemed much more legitimate.

"However, this isn't the surprise Teacher Zhang was talking about," Ying Chanxi said with a smile as she watched Teacher Zhang walk off the stage after receiving his award.

"Then what other surprise could there be?" Li Luo chuckled. "Don't tell me they're going to give me an award too?"

Ying Chanxi smiled without saying a word, simply waiting for the dean of students on stage to continue his speech.

"Besides our outstanding teachers, we of course have our outstanding students."

The dean of students looked at the students below the stage with a smile, then said, "In this graduating class, we have many excellent students."

"Among them, we have the student who has won the first prize in the Provincial Olympiad in Mathematics, first prize in the New Concept English Competition, first prize in the Science and Technology Micro-Innovation Competition, has consistently ranked first in the entire school in exams, ranked first in the independent recruitment exam for Yuhang Fuyi High School, from Class Five of the third year, student Ying Chanxi!"

"We have the student who won second prize in the Ye Shengtao Cup National New Composition Competition, first prize at the provincial level in the National Middle School Students' Innovative Composition Competition, has consistently ranked in the top three of the entire school in exams, ranked twenty-eighth in the independent recruitment exam for Yuhang Fuyi High School, from Class One of the third year, student Liu Shaowen!"

"And also..."

"..."

"And, the student who, in this high school entrance exam, forged ahead bravely and strived hard, improving by a full 130 points from his third mock exam score of 425 to achieve a high score of 555, and also received the only perfect score of 40 on the composition section of the Chinese exam in the entire school, from Class Five of the third year, student Li Luo!"

"Congratulations to these students for earning the title of Outstanding Graduates of our Yucai Middle School, Class of 2014!"

"Let us welcome these eleven students to the stage to receive their awards!"

As his voice fell, applause erupted.

Only the students of Class Five were a bit slow to react, clapping along only after a couple of seconds, their faces still a bit dazed.

What?

Li Luo?

Outstanding Graduate?

Shao Heqi turned his head in astonishment, looking at the equally dumbfounded Li Luo, his eyes filled with envy, jealousy, and hatred.

At this moment, Ying Chanxi at his side had already gracefully stood up and was waving at Li Luo with a smile.

"Silly, what are you still dazed for?"

"It's time to go on stage and get your award."
